skill.name: ace-step
skill.description: Generate, inpaint, and outpaint music with ACE Step on RunComfy via the `runcomfy` CLI. ACE Step is StepFun-AI's open-weights music foundation model — tag-driven composition (genre, mood, instruments), multilingual lyrics with section markers, 5 s to 4 min stereo output, $0.0002–0.0003 per second (≈ 27× cheaper than ElevenLabs Music). Four endpoints: ACE Step text-to-audio (the default), ACE Step 1.5 text-to-audio (50+ language lyrics, refined structured-lyric handling), ACE Step audio-inpaint (regenerate a time range inside an existing track), ACE Step audio-outpaint (extend an existing track before or after). Triggers on "ace step", "ace-step", "acestep", "ACE music", "open music model", "cheap AI music", "inpaint audio", "audio inpaint", "extend music", "audio outpaint", "lengthen track", "music with tags", or any explicit ask to generate or edit music with ACE Step.
skill.summary: Create music from tags and lyrics, replace timed sections, and extend tracks through the RunComfy CLI.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: All 96 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, legitimate documentation links, placeholder audio URLs, credential-storage guidance, or endpoint-selection prose. One semantic concern remains: the shell-safety claim overlooks single-quote escaping when adapting examples to user input. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or system reconnaissance in the supplied file; external CLI behavior was not verified.

remediation.issue: The shell-safety claim ignores shell parsing before the CLI receives JSON arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the absolute claim with explicit shell-escaping guidance. Pass serialized JSON through a shell-free argument array or correctly escape shell arguments, including apostrophes.

semantic_findings.title: Shell-Safety Assurance Omits Argument Escaping
semantic_findings.description: The skill asserts 'No shell-injection surface from prompt content' while examples wrap JSON in shell single quotes. Unescaped apostrophes in substituted lyrics, tags, or URLs can terminate those quotes before CLI parsing, potentially enabling command execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples and absolute safety claim visibly omit shell-argument escaping. Exploitation depends on unsafe substitution by the agent; no executable interpolation wrapper is supplied.

content.user_title: Create and Edit Music with ACE Step
content.value_statement: Music drafts often need new sections, alternate lyrics, or longer arrangements. This skill guides ACE Step generation and timed edits through the RunComfy CLI.
actual_capabilities: Guide tag-driven instrumental or vocal generation using ACE Step base and ACE Step 1.5 endpoints.
Structure lyrics with Verse, Chorus, Bridge, and Outro markers, with multilingual guidance for ACE Step 1.5.
Replace a selected time range in existing audio using start-relative or end-relative timing.
Extend existing tracks with new intro sections, outro sections, or both.
Configure documented duration and seed parameters, and direct generated audio downloads to a local output directory.
Explain CLI authentication requirements and documented exit codes for common failures.
limitations: Requires a separately installed RunComfy CLI, authentication, network access, and paid service usage.
Provides instructions and examples, not bundled audio models, executable wrappers, or verified CLI security controls.
Documents generation limits of 5 to 240 seconds per call and requires HTTPS source audio for editing.
Cannot guarantee musical quality, exact lyric delivery, seamless loops, or rights clearance for supplied material.

use_cases.title: Draft Background Music
use_cases.description: Explore instrumental variations using genre, mood, instrument, and tempo tags before choosing a longer render.

use_cases.title: Prepare Multilingual Song Drafts
use_cases.description: Use ACE Step 1.5 with consistent tags and language-specific lyrics to explore alternate vocal versions.

use_cases.title: Repair and Extend Arrangements
use_cases.description: Replace a weak section by timestamp or add an intro and outro around an existing hook.

prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a 30-second mellow piano instrumental using ACE Step base. Show tags, duration, and estimated service cost before submitting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a short instrumental draft.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Structured Vocal Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a 60-second Spanish indie-pop draft with ACE Step 1.5. Organize my supplied lyrics into Verse and Chorus sections. Request approval before submission.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: use multilingual lyrics and song sections.

prompt_templates.title: Replace a Timed Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my provided HTTPS audio URL to replace seconds 20 through 40 with a soft piano bridge. Preserve surrounding style. Confirm settings before submission.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: inpaint a specific region of existing audio.

prompt_templates.title: Extend a Hook with Controlled Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a 30-second intro and 60-second outro around my 30-second hook using outpainting. Set seed 42. Review duration and safely quote inputs before submission.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine bidirectional extension with explicit parameters.

output_examples.input: Add a 30-second intro and a 60-second outro to my 30-second hook.
output: Extension: 30 seconds before and 60 seconds after the source hook.
Tags will describe the new sections. Review source permissions and service cost before submission.

best_practices: Start with short drafts and specific genre, mood, instrument, and tempo tags before requesting longer renders.
Confirm source-audio rights, service costs, and the exact edit window before submitting a remote request.
Serialize inputs and safely escape shell arguments, including apostrophes; never include API tokens in prompts or logs.
anti_patterns: Submitting vague tags or omitting an instrumental marker when vocals are unwanted.
Requesting untimed inpainting edits or extensions beyond the documented total-duration limit.
Inserting raw lyrics or URLs into shell commands without proper argument escaping.

faq.question: Does this skill generate music locally?
faq.answer: No. It guides commands that submit requests to RunComfy and download the resulting audio through a separately installed CLI.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI and authenticate through runcomfy login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN. Network access and service usage charges apply.

faq.question: When should I choose ACE Step 1.5?
faq.answer: The skill recommends ACE Step 1.5 for multilingual vocals and structured lyrics. It recommends the base endpoint for lower-cost drafts.

faq.question: Can I change only part of an existing track?
faq.answer: Yes. Inpainting targets a time range using start and end values. The source must be available through an HTTPS audio URL.

faq.question: Can I add both an intro and an outro?
faq.answer: Yes. Outpainting supports extensions before and after the source. The skill advises keeping the resulting track within four minutes.

faq.question: Is passing JSON sufficient to prevent shell injection?
faq.answer: No. Shell parsing happens before CLI input processing. Use shell-free argument passing or correctly escape all shell arguments, including apostrophes.
